newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan lawmakers call for probe of abduction cases.
newsitem.headline: Japan lawmakers call for probe of abduction cases.

text.p: Japanese legislators urged the government on Tuesday to investigate allegations that North Korean agents had abducted Japanese citizens to the communist state.
More than 60 legislators from Japan's ruling and opposition parties launched a "parliamentary league" on the issue and called on the United Nations for help.

The Japanese government has said as many as nine Japanese citizens may have been abducted by North Korean agents and taken to the communist country in the past while two others barely escaped kidnap attempts.

The abduction allegations came to light in February, when Japanese media quoted South Korean security officials as saying that a North Korean defector had knowledge of a Japanese girl who was abducted 20 years ago.

The defector's description of the girl closely resembled the case of Megumi Yokota, then 13, who went missing in 1977 on her way home from school in a coastal village in Niigata Prefecture, central Japan, the reports said.
"It's impossible to resolve the issue on a private level. We need help from the government," Shigeru Yokota, Megumi's father, told reporters on Tuesday.
The kidnap reports said the victims were put to work giving Japanese language training to North Korean agents so that they could travel to carry out sabotage attacks.
State-run media in North Korea have repeatedly denied the kidnap allegations.
